newsitem.title: PERU: Hostages freed after 126 days in captivity in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Hostages freed after 126 days in captivity in Peru.

text.p: These are the names and titles of the 72 hostages, all of them men, held for 126 days by Marxist rebels at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima:
Morihisa Aoki, Japan's ambassador to Peru.
Jorge Gumucio, Bolivia's ambassador to Peru.
Pedro Fujimori, brother of Peru's President Alberto Fujimori.
Ricardo Kamiya, Peruvian presidency secretary general.
Juan Mendoza, Peru's deputy mines minister.
Salvador Romero, Energy and Mines Ministry secretary.
Luis Giampetri, Navy vice admiral and president of the National Institute of the Peruvian Sea.
Gen. Maximo Rivera, head of Peru's anti-terrorism police DINCOTE.
Gen. Alfonso Villanueva, head of police intelligence.
Guillermo Bobio, chief of state security.
Police Gen. Julio Pinto, scretary of the National Police directorate.
Police Gen. Hugo Vera, police economy director.
Police Col. Jaime Valencia, head of the police kidnapping division.
Police Col. Marco Miyashiro, former head of DINCOTE intelligence.
Father Juan Julio Wicht, Roman Catholic priest and economy professor at Lima's Pacific University.
Miguel Takahasi, adviser to Peruvian state fishing firm Pescaperu.
Jose Ishiki, accountant for Cogorno food firm.
Tokeshi Gusukuda, researcher for the Centre for Development Promotion.
Jaime Bisso, manager of Peruvian bank Banco Regional del Norte.
Shiguero Taki, director general of Panasonic.
Kosabe Shoji, engineer for NOys company.
Fumio Sunami, Japanese embassy first secretary
